newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan seen importing sugar next year.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan seen importing sugar next year.

text.p: Pakistani sugar mill owners gave conflicting estimates of the 1996/97 sugar crop on Wednesday, with some saying Pakistan may have to import up to 300,000 tonnes to make up a production shortfall.
Ali Qizilbash, secretary general of the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association (PSMA), said he was confident production would balance demand, but other mill owners had doubts.
"Pakistan is likely to produce 2.7 million tonnes of sugar in 1996/97 (July-June), which is enough to meet the country's requirement of slightly more than 2.6 million tonnes," Qizilbash told Reuters.
Pakistan produced 2.47 million tonnes in 1995/96, less than usual because many farmers had switched to cotton for better returns.

Mill owner Mohammad Ebrahim Hasham said prospects of hitting the target of 2.7 million tonnes this year were dim because the crop appeared to be about 10 percent down on last year, and extraction rates of sugar from sugarcane were falling.
The PSMA said the recovery rate dropped to 9.19 percent in 1995/96 from 9.65 percent in 1994/95.
"I think Pakistan will have to import 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes of sugar to meet the shortfall," Hasham said.

Final production figures will not be known until the end of the sugarcane crushing season in May. Mill owners have delayed until next month the start of the crushing season, which normally begins in October, to allow the crop to fully ripen.

Hasham forecast that the crop in the southern province of Sindh would be 15 percent less than last year because of reduced rainfall. The crop in Punjab province would exceed last year's by five percent because of slightly higher rainfall.
Dealers said sugar demand was rising in Pakistan, partly because of rampant smuggling to neighbouring Iran and Afghanistan, which in turn sell sugar to Central Asian states.
"The demand for sugar is continuously rising in Central Asia," said one dealer.

Pakistan had signed import deals for 375,000 tonnes of sugar -- 225,000 tonnes bought by the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) and 150,000 tonnes by the private sector -- to meet a shortfall in the past three months, Hasham said.
A TCP official, who asked not to be named, said the government was keeping a strict watch on the supply and demand equation, but had no immediate plans to import more sugar.
Eight ships laden with some 93,000 tonnes of sugar were awaiting berths at Karachi Port on Tuesday, port officials said.
